WHEREAS, the Town Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia is authorized by Art. IX, § II, [ Ul of the Constitution of the State of Georgia of 1983, to enact ordinances for the health, safety and welfare of the general public; and

WHEREAS, pursuant to O.C.G.A. §§ 48-13-1 and 48-13-5, et seq., the Town Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia, adopted an Occupational Tax Ordinance on December 22, 1994 for the Town of Clermont, Georgia, and amended said ordinance on December 26, 1995; and

WHEREAS, the Town Council desires to amend said ordinance to provide for additional penalties for violation of the ordinance;

NOW, THEREFORE, the Mayor and Council of the Town of Clermont, Georgia hereby ordains, and it is hereby ordained by authority of same, as follows:

(A) Each such business tax shall be for the calendar year 1995 and succeeding calendar years thereafter unless otherwise specifically provided. Said registration and occupation tax shall be payable on January 1 of each year and shall be delinquent if not paid by April 1 of each year and be subject to penalties for delinquency as described in this ordinance. On any new profession, trade or calling begun in the Town in 1995 or succeeding years thereafter, the registration and tax shall be delinquent if not obtained immediately upon beginning business and a ten (10%) penalty shall be imposed if not paid within ninety (90) days of the commencement 0 the business. The tax certificate herein provided for shall be issued by the Town Clerk and if any person, firm, or corporation whose duty it is to obtain a registration shall, after said registration or occupational tax becomes delinquent, transact, or offer to transact, in the Town, any of the kind of profession, trade or calling in this ordinance specified without having first obtained said registration, such offender shall, in addition to the penalties and remedies provided herein, upon conviction, be punished as provided in Section 34 of this ordinance.

(B) In addition to the above remedies, the Town, through a proper agent, including, but not limited to the Town Attorney, may proceed to collect in the same manner as provided by law for tax executions, all delinquent taxes, penalties, interest, fines and forfeitures assessed pursuant to this ordinance.

Any person (which shall include but not limited to, in the case of, corporate entities, partnerships, or other forms of business organization, the officer or agent soliciting for or

representing such persons, as also provided by Section 14 of this ordinance) violating any provision of this ordinance shall, upon conviction, be assessed a fine up to a maximum of $1,000.00, or subject to confinement up to six months, or both, as assessed by any acting judge (including but not limited to any Hall County Magistrate or other judge of a court of competent jurisdiction) of the Municipal Court of the Town of Clermont for said violation. Further, as imposed and assessed by the J udge of the Municipal Court of the Town of Clermont, any person given confinement in the municipal court may work out such sentences by the performance of community service by public works on behalf of the Town of Clermont, Georgia, or on the streets, roads, drains, and squares or other public property in the City. Such penalties may be in addition to the other penalties provided by this ordinance, including the ten (10%) percent penalty and interest imposed by this ordinance. The continued willful operation of any profession, trade or calling, without having received an occupational tax certificate or license from the Town as provided herein, or failing to have and obtain any health permits, bonds, certificates of qualification, certificates of competency, or any other regulatory matter imposed by the State of Georgia, by the local government of Hall County, Georgia, or of any of their entities, instrumentalities, departments, or agencies, or any combination thereof, shall subject the person (including agents, officers, and employees as provided herein), upon conviction, to the punishments and penalties as provided by this section of the Occupational Tax Ordinance. Each day of operation of any profession, trade or calling without a certificate or occupational tax license from the Town, or without any required health permits, bonds, certificates of qualification, certificates of competency, from either the State of Georgia, or Hall County,

Georgia, or any of their departments, agencies, entities, or instrumentalities, or any combination

thereof, shall be deemed to be a separate violation of this ordinance, with each separate violation subject to the penalties allowed and provided by this section of the ordinance.
